annotation.title_clean: The typification of infringement issues of humanoid robots: with special reference to the governance of infringement caused by learning algorithms
annotation.title_en: The typification of infringement issues of humanoid robots: with special reference to the governance of infringement caused by learning algorithms
annotation.summary_en: Chinese legal article typifying humanoid robot infringement into passive and active types, focusing on harm from learning algorithms. Using law and economics and the Hand Formula, it allocates liability among manufacturers, users and general AI model providers, who may be jointly liable if they fail on transparency.
key_provisions_or_claims: Humanoid robots' human-like appearance, intelligence and mixed control create an anthropomorphic trap and expand infringement risk.
Infringement divides into passive and active types, with further subtypes.
Learning-algorithm failures are the most distinctive type, given the 'autonomous safety paradox'.
Manufacturers' duties follow dynamic regulations guided by the Hand Formula.
Users bear liability for negligence in reasonable care; general AI model providers may be jointly liable for transparency failures.
